title: "Research"
subtitle: "How we measure political beliefs, and what those measurements can tell us"

My research brings together political theory, data science and statistical methods, with interests spanning computational international relations, political theory, predictive modelling and machine learning. Right now I'm part of the [Data Impact Lab](https://data-impact.pages.dev/).

::: {.entry .open data-when="2026"}
### Evaluating language models with political psychology scales

::: {.meta}
Large language models, psychometrics, political psychology
:::

I'm investigating how we evaluate large language models using established political psychology scales: what it means for a model to "hold" a political attitude, and how far measurement tools built for people can be trusted when they are applied to AI.
:::

::: {.entry data-when="2026"}
### Facial expression studies

::: {.meta}
Data Impact Lab, with Dr Jie Kang and Prof Ted Ruffman (University of Otago)
:::

- Finished the statistical analysis.
- Two manuscripts in preparation, for the *Journal of Nonverbal Behavior* and *Cognition and Emotion*.
:::

::: {.entry data-when="2026"}
### Civics Education and Truth-Readiness: An International Comparative Analysis

::: {.meta}
Sydney Policy Reform Project (recipient, 2026), Faculty of Arts and Social Sciences, University of Sydney
:::

- Co-authoring a policy paper for ANTAR under academic supervision.
- Contributing research to policy and law reform for community organisations and public agencies.

::: {.entry data-when="2025"}
### Statistical modelling for policy-making

::: {.meta}
Charles Perkins Centre Summer Research Scholarship
:::

- Built an OLS predictive model to support policy-making.
- Provided the theoretical framework, drawing on Samuel Moyn's critique of human rights and Elizabeth Anderson's *Private Government*.
- Supervised by A/Prof Clara Grazian (Mathematics & Statistics) and Prof Alexandre Lefebvre (Politics & Philosophy).
:::

:::
